newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police nab boys over "virtual pet" heist.
newsitem.headline: Japan police nab boys over "virtual pet" heist.

text.p: Japanese police took four teenage boys into custody on Friday over the suspected theft of an electronic "virtual pet" game that has become a craze among Japanese youth.
Police in Yokohama, south of Tokyo, said they had detained the 14-year-old junior high school boys after a chase involving a police helicopter and several patrol cars.
The four are suspected of forcing a fellow student to hand over his "Tamagocchi", a highly prized key-ring game featuring an electronic bird-like creature.
After receiving an emergency call from the victim, police said they chased the four boys to a shopping area in Yokohama, with a police helicopter helping in surveillance.
The alleged victim, also 14, accused the four of stealing another Tamagocchi game from him last week, police said.
Japanese laws prohibit the identification of minors suspected of committing a crime.

The Tamagocchi game has been a complete sell-out in Japan and the maker has said fresh supplies will not be available until April. On the streets and on the Internet, second-hand units are being hawked at between 20 to 30 times their retail price of 1,980 yen ($16).

The aim of the game, which is made by toymaker Bandai Co Ltd, is to raise and nurture the creature on the key-ring display using electronic commands. The creature, whose lifespan depends on the quality of care provided, can be fed and stroked and "goes to the bathroom" -- in an electronic sense -- just like a live pet. It will "die" if neglected.
